proposals.name: Binary-source microlens event
proposals.idea: An unseen foreground point lens first magnified a hot, blue background star, producing the smooth roughly 35-day g-band rise and much faster symmetric fall that the slow TDE decline overpredicted. A short second magnification of a red companion is now adding the abrupt r-band light, represented by the flare on a steady baseline, while the blue magnification continues to fade.
proposals.predicts: It predicts g returns symmetrically toward its pre-event baseline rather than staying bright and blue, while r peaks within a few days and then fades rapidly as the brief red flare ends.

proposals.name: Microlensing with lens-star flare
proposals.idea: An unseen low-mass object in the Galactic plane point-lenses a hot background source, producing the symmetric, very blue g-band rise and fall that a TDE power law cannot match. The lens is a red dwarf whose brief flare supplies the sudden r-band brightening near day -1 while g keeps fading.
proposals.predicts: It predicts a symmetric return of g to its faint pre-event baseline within weeks and a days-long decay of the r-only spike, instead of the TDE's lingering bright blue power-law tail.

proposals.name: Crowded-field template PSF ghost
proposals.idea: At low Galactic latitude a bright neighbour in the g reference template is imperfectly PSF-matched, so seeing and pointing drift create a g-only subtraction residual that waxes smoothly and then wanes while the cleaner r reference remains blank. The isolated late r detection is a brief residual from the same mismatched neighbour, not a real reddening source.
proposals.predicts: It predicts both bands settle within days to the flat pre-event baseline, with the r point disappearing as quickly as it appeared and no sustained achromatic TDE-like brightening.

proposals.name: Blue explosion with red flare
proposals.idea: A blue explosion peaked near day -24 and is now declining symmetrically, rather than maintaining a TDE-like power-law tail. A separate short-lived, very red hidden source switched on near day -1, producing the isolated bright r point with little extra g light.
proposals.predicts: g will continue its rapid exponential fade toward baseline while the r excess peaks around now and disappears within a few days, leaving no bright blue plateau.

proposals.name: Cooling double-peaked explosion
proposals.idea: The g-band event is hot ejecta that peaked near day -24 and is now cooling and fading, not a still-rising accretion flow. Slower, cooler, more opaque ejecta are producing a delayed red peak, on top of faint steady host light.
proposals.predicts: It predicts g keeps fading while r peaks later and declines more slowly, so the source stays red and returns to baseline rather than resuming a blue TDE rise.
